proposals.rule: You must pay the healthcare surcharge for each year of your stay
proposals.exception: If you’re a doctor or nurse, or you work in health or adult social care, check if you’re eligible to apply for the Health and Care Worker visa instead. It’s cheaper to apply for and you do not need to pay the annual immigration health surcharge.
proposals.why: The exception applies to doctors, nurses, or health/social care workers who can use the Health and Care Worker visa and avoid the surcharge.

proposals.rule: You cannot extend your Graduate visa.
proposals.exception: You may be able to extend your visa if you’re eligible, for example to continue your studies in the UK.
proposals.why: B applies to Student visa extensions, not to Graduate visa, providing a narrower case where extension is possible.

proposals.rule: You can apply for a Youth Mobility Scheme visa if you: have £2,530 in savings
proposals.exception: You must have at least £2,530 in your bank account to show you can support yourself in the UK. You will need to have had the money available for at least 28 days in a row.
proposals.why: The exception narrows the savings requirement to a minimum balance that must have been held for 28 consecutive days.

proposals.rule: You’ll need to provide proof of your finances, if you’re not applying on the basis of your private life
proposals.exception: You do not need to meet a minimum income requirement if your partner gets one of the following benefits: Disability Living Allowance, Scottish Adult Disability Living Allowance, Severe Disablement Allowance, Industrial Injuries Disablement Benefit, Attendance Allowance, Pension Age Disability Payment, Carer’s Allowance, Carer Support Payment, Personal Independence Payment, Armed Forces Independence Payment or Guaranteed Income Payment under the Armed Forces Compensation Scheme, Constant Attendance Allowance, Mobility Supplement or War Disablement Pension under the War Pensions Scheme, Police Injury Pension, Child Disability Payment, Adult Disability Payment
proposals.why: The exception applies only when the partner receives specified disability or carer benefits, thereby waiving the general financial proof requirement

proposals.rule: You may be able to apply for settlement once you’ve been in the UK for 3 years.
proposals.exception: You must have a new endorsement that shows you’ve met the requirements for growing your business
proposals.why: The settlement eligibility is narrowed to those who have a new endorsement after 3 years of residence

proposals.rule: A dependent partner and dependent children can apply on this route.
proposals.exception: Dependent partners and children can apply on this route (with some exceptions for dependants of care workers, senior care workers and medium skilled roles) as set out in the: Dependants guidance
proposals.why: The exception narrows the rule to exclude dependants of care workers, senior care workers and medium skilled roles.

proposals.rule: You can stay for 3 years if you either: come to the UK on an Innovator Founder visa or switch to this visa from another visa while in the UK
proposals.exception: An applicant who is in the UK cannot apply to switch into the Innovator Founder route if they have, or were last granted, permission as any of the following: as a Visitor, as a Short-term Student, as a Parent of a Child Student, as a Seasonal Worker, as a domestic worker in a private household
proposals.why: The exception narrows the switching rule to exclude applicants who previously held certain types of UK permission

proposals.rule: (a) be studying a full-time course of study leading to the award of a PhD with a higher education provider which has a track record of compliance; and (ii) have completed at least 24 months of study on that course.
proposals.exception: If the course was leading to a PhD award they must have completed at least 12 months of that course.
proposals.why: The exception narrows the PhD study requirement from 24 months to 12 months for applicants who have completed a PhD course.

proposals.rule: You can study, do a placement or take an exam
proposals.exception: If you are coming to the UK to study as a Visitor, you must also meet the additional requirements at V 9.1. to V 9.5
proposals.why: The exception narrows the general study permission to those studying as a Visitor, adding extra eligibility requirements

proposals.rule: A Standard Visitor may apply for a visit visa of six months, two, five or 10 years validity, however each stay in the UK must not exceed the permitted length of stay endorsed on the visit visa (usually six months).
proposals.exception: If your treatment will last longer than 6 months All visits for medical treatment lasting longer than 6 months require a Standard Visitor visa regardless of your nationality.
proposals.why: The exception allows stays longer than the usual 6‑month limit for medical treatment, extending the stay to up to 11 months or more.

proposals.rule: You can work in most jobs
proposals.exception: no employment as a professional sportsperson (including as a sports coach)
proposals.why: exception narrows to professional sportspersons, excluding them from the general work allowance

proposals.rule: With a Graduate visa you can: work in most jobs
proposals.exception: work (including self-employment and voluntary work) is permitted, apart from work as a professional sportsperson
proposals.why: excludes work as a professional sportsperson

proposals.rule: You cannot apply to change (‘switch’) to a Graduate Trainee visa from inside the UK.
proposals.exception: Existing Intra-Company workers can apply for extensions and changes of employment under the Senior or Specialist Worker and Graduate Trainee routes.
proposals.why: The exception applies only to workers who already have permission on the legacy Intra‑Company routes, allowing them to change to the Graduate Trainee route from within the UK.

proposals.rule: You can stay in the UK with a UK Expansion Worker visa for whichever is shorter of: 12 months after the start date of the job on your certificate of sponsorship the time given on your certificate of sponsorship plus 14 days If you want to stay longer in the UK, you can extend your visa by 12 months. The maximum time you can stay in the UK on a UK Expansion Worker visa is 2 years.
proposals.exception: You can only stay in the UK for a maximum of 5 years in any 6 year period if you’ve spent time on any of these visas: Intra-company Graduate Trainee visa Intra-company Transfer visa Graduate Trainee visa (Global Business Mobility) Secondment Worker visa (Global Business Mobility) Senior or Specialist Worker visa (Global Business Mobility) Service Supplier visa (Global Business Mobility) UK Expansion Worker visa (Global Business Mobility)
proposals.why: The exception narrows the stay limit to a 5‑year cap over 6 years for applicants who have previously held certain UK visas, overriding the 2‑year cap for new Expansion Worker visa

proposals.rule: You can come to the UK for a maximum of up to 12 months, or the time given in your certificate of sponsorship plus up to 28 days, whichever is shorter.
proposals.exception: You can stay for up to 12 months or the time given on your certificate of sponsorship plus 14 days, whichever is shorter.
proposals.why: The charity worker visa limits the extra days to 14 instead of 28.

proposals.rule: If you’re an overseas government worker or international organisation worker, you can stay for up to 2 years or the time given on your certificate of sponsorship plus up to 14 days, whichever is shorter.
proposals.exception: You can stay in the UK: up to 6 months for horticulture work
proposals.why: exception covers horticulture work, limiting stay to 6 months

proposals.rule: You can come to the UK for a maximum of up to 12 months, or the time given in your certificate of sponsorship plus up to 28 days, whichever is shorter.
proposals.exception: You can stay in the UK: up to 6 months for horticulture work
proposals.why: The Seasonal Worker visa limits horticulture work to a maximum of 6 months, which is a narrower time window than the 12‑month limit for Creative Workers.

proposals.rule: After 6 months you can change or stop doing your job without telling the Home Office
proposals.exception: During the first 6 months of your stay you cannot change employer unless you apply to update your visa
proposals.why: exception covers the first 6 months, restricting the ability to change employer that the rule allows after 6 months

proposals.rule: Your partner and children can also apply to join you or stay in the UK as your ‘dependants’ if they’re eligible.
proposals.exception: Your partner or children cannot apply to switch to your Scale-up Worker visa as your dependants if they are currently in the UK: on a visit visa
proposals.why: The exception narrows the rule to exclude partners or children who are on a visit visa at the time of application.

proposals.rule: Removing foreign transaction fees for Reward and Premier Reward debit cards (General Term 7.4)
proposals.exception: Debit card payment in a foreign currency • Non‑Sterling Transaction Fee 2.75% of transaction
proposals.why: The exception applies only to the Reward account, where a foreign‑currency transaction fee is charged, contrary to the general rule that such fees are removed for Reward and Premie

proposals.rule: You can only have one Reward Platinum account in your sole name.
proposals.exception: You can have more than one joint Reward Platinum account, as long as the other account holder is different on each one.
proposals.why: The exception allows multiple Reward Platinum accounts when held jointly with different partners, which is a narrower case than the sole‑name rule.

proposals.rule: With a Reward Silver account, you won't pay any non-sterling transaction fees when paying with your debit card anywhere in the world.
proposals.exception: Not valid for ATM withdrawals.
proposals.why: The exception limits the fee‑free benefit to card payments only, excluding ATM withdrawals.

proposals.rule: Most of our accounts (except our Basic Bank Account) come with an interest‑free amount.
proposals.exception:
Bank Account
34.05%
39.9% EAR variable
No interest on the first £25 of your arranged or unarranged overdraft.
proposals.why: The exception applies only to the standard Bank Account, specifying the exact interest‑free amount (£25) and overriding the general rule for all other accounts.

proposals.rule: From 20 June 2023, we removed the 1|2|3 Current Account and Select Current Account from our product range.
proposals.exception: From 11 May 2026, we’re increasing the monthly fee on our 1|2|3, Select and Private current accounts from £4 to £5.
proposals.why: The exception applies to existing 1|2|3 and Select accounts that are still held, while the rule applies to new customers who can no longer open those accounts.

proposals.rule: If you cancel Extra you’ll lose access to its benefits, but we’ll keep your Monzo Current Account open.
proposals.exception: If you cancel Extra you can continue using your benefits until your next payment date, but you won’t get a refund.
proposals.why: covers cancellations after the 14‑day cooling‑off period

proposals.rule: If you cancel Extra you’ll lose access to its benefits, but we’ll keep your Monzo Current Account open.
proposals.exception: If you cancel Extra you can continue using your benefits until your next payment date, but you won’t get a refund.
proposals.why: covers cancellations after the 14‑day cooling‑off period

proposals.rule: After 14 days, but within 6 months of signing up £50 fee (if you've ordered a metal card). We'll refund you for any remaining days in the month you cancel.
proposals.exception: After your 6-month minimum terms ends No fee. We'll refund you for any remaining days in the month you cancel.
proposals.why: The exception applies only after the 6‑month minimum term has ended, a narrower time window where the cancellation fee is waived.
